### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `492d494c4f0c0f98d0d2d8418e1eaccdc2a06693` — the merge of head `06329b0ae051b5558f3fa07a8a1ba34c6c6902ad` into base `e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 492d494c4f0c0f98d0d2d8418e1eaccdc2a06693 && git checkout 492d494c4f0c0f98d0d2d8418e1eaccdc2a06693
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 06329b0ae051b5558f3fa07a8a1ba34c6c6902ad && git checkout -B drift-repro e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574 && git merge --no-ff 06329b0ae051b5558f3fa07a8a1ba34c6c6902ad

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e40cd1e28dd79e60e7f4be0db06f071f3f962574` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d8d72cf5d10eeac9e446ac500339e2965296990d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-account-key.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-standard-claims.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, .changeset/33437-saml-stable-account-key.md, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx + the two test files

### ① Derived judgments

- **The adapter rewrite holds as the contract point (your question).** It is scoped three ways: to `sys_account` only, to the ACS request whose preview reading exists, and to a where clause that is all equalities naming this provider id and this NameID. Every other read and write is handed back unchanged, and a read of the user's accounts by `userId` is never rewritten. The write half rewrites only a row for this provider and NameID. The pre-read is safe because #33418 admits exactly one Assertion, so the preview and the vendor's verified extract read the same element. The fallback is the NameID whenever the attribute is not one plain text value.
- **The confirmation covers every path that binds an account.** In better-auth 1.7.12 `handleOAuthUserInfo`, `assertValidUserInfo` runs with `action: "sign-in"` for a found linked account, with `action: "link-account"` before `linkAccount`, and on the create path. `refuseSamlAccountKeyContradiction` runs first in `validateUserInfo` and compares the verified extract with the reading. So a key read from an unsigned or commented part of the XML cannot bind anything; the comment pin measures that.
- **must-fix M1: the legacy-account sentence in BREAKING is unmeasured, and it is narrower than it reads.** Traced against the vendor at this head, a legacy Entra account (row `(provider, NameID-at-creation)`) behaves like this:
  1. **Same NameID, same email: signs in, nothing new written.** `findAccountOwnerByKey` is rewritten to the object id and misses, so the user is found by email. Then `dbUser.accounts.find(acc => acc.accountId === account.accountId)` matches in memory, because the vendor's `account.accountId` is still the NameID (the rewrite lives in the adapter, not in the vendor's value). This works only through that in-memory compare.
  2. **Other entry (a different NameID), same email: the linking rule, as before.** No row matches, so the implicit-link gate decides. With SAML's `trustProviderByName: false`, it links only if the provider is `domainVerified` for that domain or `trustEmailVerified` is on, and the local email is verified. Otherwise the answer is `account not linked`. So for a legacy account, the bug #33437 fixes stays.
  3. **Email changed at the IdP: a new user.** No user has the new email, so with JIT on a second user is created with an object-id-keyed row; with JIT off it is refused. The old account is not reached.

  None of these three has a pin (the 13 new cases all start from an empty `sys_account`). The text says the person "still signs in when the email ... is that account's email". That is true only for case 1. Please (a) add pins that seed a legacy NameID-keyed row and measure cases 1 to 3; and (b) make the sentence say what they measure. For example: the legacy account still signs in from the entry it was made with while its email is unchanged; a sign-in from the other entry is judged by the linking rule as before (so #33437 stays for those accounts); an email change at the IdP makes a new account (or is refused without JIT). The doc's "Key accounts on a stable attribute" section owes the same sentence. A delta that adds those pins and that text converts this to PASS.
- **nit N1.** The help text and doc say "stable" and "immutable". Please add that the attribute must be one the IdP sets and the person cannot edit. A user-editable attribute named as the key lets a person sign in as whoever's value they type. One clause is enough.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` and `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch` are correct for a non-protocol change. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the widening in prose, `!`, BREAKING and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are all present, and the marker's reason (decision B: existing rows not rewritten) matches.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Vendor coupling: the rewrite depends on better-auth 1.7.12 finding the owner by an equality where on `(providerId, accountId)`, and on the in-memory account compare using the vendor's own value. A vendor bump that changes either shape silently undoes the key, or case 1 above. The pins in M1(a) are what catches that.
- Security: the key binds an account, so N1 matters. Nothing here goes to the advisory track.
- The PR is a draft with CI running (read at this head: 36 success, 15 skipped, 1 in progress). The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head. As a narrowing arm, it also owes the dogfood battery.

### ④ Design judgment

Keying at the adapter, with a confirmation at the vendor's one validation hook, is the smallest design that keeps the vendor's lookup, linking rule and create path unchanged. The alternative, forking the SSO callback to pass a different account id, would own far more vendor code. Leaving existing rows alone is decision B. The design holds. The FAIL is M1: the operator-facing sentence about existing accounts has to be measured and say what it measures.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `06329b0ae051b5558f3fa07a8a1ba34c6c6902ad`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/33437-saml-stable-account-key.md, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts + 21 regenerated translation files

This reviews the delta `d8d72cf5...06329b0a` on my FAIL at `d8d72cf5d10eeac9e446ac500339e2965296990d`. It is one commit: four hand-edited files and 21 regenerated translation files. No `src` code under plugin-auth changed. Every other file is as I read it at `d8d72cf5`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 closed.**
  - **The pins.** Three real-stack pins seed a legacy row: `sys_account (PROVIDER_ID, UPN)` for an unverified, JIT-made `usr_legacy`. Each measures one case of my trace:
    1. Same NameID and email: signs in to `usr_legacy`, and nothing new is written.
    2. Portal entry (opaque NameID): `account_not_linked` on the console login page, with no session and nothing written.
    3. Email changed at the IdP, NameID unchanged (`renamed` spreads `spInitiated`, so `nameID` stays the UPN): with JIT, a second user is made keyed on the object id, and no session goes to `usr_legacy`. Without JIT, the answer is `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` and nothing is written.
  - **The text.** The changeset's Clause-② clause, the BREAKING list and the sso.mdx "Accounts made before" bullet now state exactly those three cases. The text also says, correctly, that #33437 is not fixed for legacy accounts, and that case 3 signed in to the old account before this change.
  - **Vendor coupling.** Case 1 is the pin I asked for, because it rests on the vendor's in-memory compare of `dbUser.accounts`.
- **N1 closed.** The `mapAccountKey` help text, the doc table row and the doc's numbered rule now say the attribute must be one the IdP sets and the user cannot edit. They name the object id and the Okta user id as examples, exclude email, name and profile fields, and give the reason (whoever holds the value holds the account).
- The 21 translation files are the regenerated source hashes and objects for the changed help text.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, `fix(auth)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the widening in prose, BREAKING, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The vendor coupling is now pinned at both ends: the key lookup (the existing pins) and the legacy in-memory compare (case 1).
- CI at this head is still running (read 23:33Z: 17 success, 17 skipped, 20 in progress). The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head, including the dogfood battery this narrowing arm owes.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged from `d8d72cf5`. Keying at the adapter, with the confirmation at the vendor's validation hook, is the smallest sound design, and leaving existing rows alone is decision B.
